title: Handoff contract
description: A lightweight contract format for quality expectations at the handoffs between people and AI agents. Draft v0.2 — expect breaking changes. Most fields are optional by design (lazy elaboration): a minimal contract should cost almost nothing to author, gaining specificity only where a collaboration has demonstrated it needs it.

handoff_contract.description: Schema version this document conforms to.

quality_spectrum.description: Where this project sits between speed and polish. The single tacit assumption most likely to wreck a zero-history handoff.

quality_notes.description: What the spectrum position means for THIS project.

glossary.description: Contested terms, defined once (e.g., what 'strategist' means on this team).

role.description: Plain-language role, not a job title.

requires.description: Element 2 of 5: what you must give me to begin.

blocking.description: Can I start without it? For agent contributors, blocking inputs fail closed.

returns.description: Element 3 of 5: the deliverable, named concretely.

done_looks_like.description: Element 4 of 5: acceptance criteria at MY handoff point.

intended_use.description: Element 5 of 5 — the fitness clause, forward-looking: what is THIS deliverable for? Added in v0.2.

not_for.description: Contraindications: contexts where a deliverable like this is not recommended. The highest-leverage field — negative space is sharper than positive description.

exemplar.description: The quality anchor: a prior deliverable this work should be calibrated against.

provenance.description: The fitness clause, backward-looking: what was the exemplar for? An exemplar can be faithfully imitated and still wrong if applied outside its provenance. Added in v0.2.

annotations.description: Director's commentary: which choices were deliberate, which were imposed, and what a weaker version looked like.

delta.description: Departures from the exemplar, in a constrained vocabulary. The fixed dimension set is deliberate: free-text deltas reintroduce the ambiguity the contract exists to remove, so unknown keys are invalid here.

depth.description: Rigor: how far down each thread goes.

notes.description: Free text — last resort, flagged in review.

calibration.description: How this contract was derived. Self-reports are systematically optimistic; interview-derived contracts are the elicitation bet this format makes.

optimism_flags.description: Known planning-fallacy zones for this contributor and deliverable type.

handoff.description: Who receives the work, and how divergence is handled. Enforcement is deliberately asymmetric: humans get norms, agents get schemas.

checkpoint.description: 'advisory' (humans): divergence is flagged, not blocked. 'fail_closed' (agents): the agent will not proceed without its declared blocking inputs.
